name: Market Square
description: The sound hits you first — a rolling wave of voices, cart wheels, and harbor bells. The market square of the Accord of Tides is a crossroads of the southern world. Vendors call prices in three languages. The smell of fried fish and foreign spices mingles in the salt air. Somewhere nearby, a street musician is losing a competition with the gulls.
key_features: a central fountain where travelers wash road dust from their boots
a guild noticeboard thick with postings and bounty notices
the harbormaster's office with a line out the door

hidden_elements.description: a recent posting about disturbances in the Greyvale, partially covered by newer notices

time_night.description_override: The market square is emptied out. Lanterns swing on their chains. The fountain burbles to no one. A pair of city guards walk their circuit, boots echoing on wet stone.

key_features_add: a cluster of worried merchants discussing trade route disruptions to the north

name: Millhaven
description: Millhaven used to be a quiet farming town. You can hear what it should sound like — wind through barley, a mill wheel turning, children somewhere. But there's a tension underneath. Conversations drop to whispers when strangers arrive. The mill wheel needs oiling and no one's bothered. Dogs bark at the northern tree line for no visible reason.
atmosphere: pastoral unease, normality fraying at the edges
key_features: the old stone mill at the town's center, still running but neglected
a makeshift notice board with warnings about traveling north alone
a cluster of refugee families camped near the south road, recently arrived from further north
the muddy northern edge of town, where the last houses give way to open road

hidden_elements.description: unusual tracks at the northern edge of town — not animal, not human, impressions in the earth that seem to resist being looked at directly

time_night.description_override: Millhaven after dark is a town holding its breath. Shutters are closed tight, bolted from inside. A dog barks somewhere and others answer, a chain of anxiety running house to house. The mill wheel turns alone. The northern tree line is a black wall, and no one looks at it.
time_night.atmosphere: shuttered, fearful, dogs barking at nothing

quest:greyvale_anomaly:stage >= 3.atmosphere: openly frightened, people preparing to evacuate
key_features_add: townsfolk packing carts and arguing about whether to flee south

name: Greyvale Ruins — Entrance Hall
description: The stairs descend into stone that predates everything above it. The air changes — cool, still, tasting of dust and something faintly metallic. Your footsteps echo in a way that suggests a large space ahead. Light from above fades quickly. Then you hear it — a low, almost subliminal hum, as if the stone itself is vibrating at a frequency just below hearing.
key_features: Aelindran script carved into the archway — partially defaced but legible to a scholar
old sconces that once held arcane lights, now dark
a research station with scattered papers and broken glass, more recent than the ruins themselves

hidden_elements.description: a journal page wedged beneath a fallen shelf — handwriting in academic Aelindran, referencing 'resonance thinning' and a 'controlled aperture'
a ward-seal on the inner door bearing Veythar's personal sigil — not a temple mark, a private one

hollow_corruption >= 3.atmosphere_add: the hum is louder now, oscillating, and you feel it in your teeth

name: The Hollow Breach
description: You know you've arrived because the world stops. The birdsong cuts off mid-phrase. The wind dies. The grass beneath your feet is grey and brittle, crumbling at the edges like ash. And then you hear it — not a sound, exactly. An absence shaped like sound. A pressure in your ears that has no source. Something is here. Something that doesn't belong in any world you understand.
atmosphere: deeply wrong, alien silence, sensory inversion
key_features: a circle of dead earth roughly thirty paces across, the grass grey and crumbling
a shimmer in the air at the center — not light, not darkness, something the eyes refuse to process
the remains of what might have been animals, but they're wrong — too many joints, fur growing inward

hidden_elements.description: arcane residue at the breach's edge that doesn't match normal Hollow signatures — it's structured, almost deliberate, as if something was opened rather than broken through

name: Guild Hall
description: Heavy oak doors open onto a hall that smells of lamp oil, leather, and old paper. A long counter runs the length of the far wall, clerks behind it processing bounty claims and contract disputes. Notice boards flank both sides, layered deep with postings. Somewhere upstairs, raised voices argue strategy.
key_features: the main counter where contracts are filed and bounties claimed
a wall of notice boards sorted by danger rating
Torin's office door at the back, usually open

time_night.description_override: The guild hall is quieter after dark. Most clerks have gone, leaving half the lamps lit. A few night-shift contractors murmur over paperwork. Torin's office door is closed, a line of light beneath it.
time_night.atmosphere: subdued, late-working, quieter but not empty

name: Training Hall
description: Off the guild hall's north stair, a long room of worn floorboards and chalk-scuffed practice circles. Wooden weapons rest in racks along one wall; the air carries sweat, oiled leather, and the steady thock of a training dummy somewhere out of sight. A mentor watches from a stool, unhurried.
atmosphere: focused, patient, the quiet of deliberate work
key_features: chalk practice circles worn into the floor
racks of blunted practice weapons
a mentor who measures you with a glance

name: Temple Row
description: A wide avenue lined with temples to the four gods. Incense drifts from open doorways. Acolytes sweep steps in the early light. The architecture shifts every few dozen paces — Veythar's sharp angles giving way to Kaelen's flowing curves, then Aelora's open arches, then Syrath's shadowed alcoves.
key_features: four distinct temples, each reflecting their god's aesthetic
a shared meditation garden at the avenue's center
pilgrims and petitioners waiting outside various doors

time_night.description_override: Candlelight spills from temple doorways onto empty steps. The avenue is contemplative at night — distant chanting carries from Aelora's temple, and the incense is stronger in the stillness. A lone acolyte tends a shrine by lantern.

name: Dockside Quarter
description: Salt spray and tar. Ropes creak against wooden hulls. The dockside quarter is where the Accord's real business happens — cargo manifests, contraband, and rumors from every port on the Sunward Coast. Warehouses line the waterfront, and between them, scholars' workshops where the Aelindran diaspora study recovered artifacts.
key_features: the main wharf where merchant vessels dock
a row of scholars' workshops in converted warehouses
Emris's research station near the eastern pier

time_night.description_override: The docks are different at night. Watchmen replace dockworkers, lanterns sway on moored masts. The water is black and still, reflecting orange light. Somewhere a cargo hatch creaks in the wind. The scholars' workshops are dark, but one window still glows.

name: The Hearthstone Tavern
description: Warmth hits you first — a wall of heat from the massive stone hearth that gives this place its name. Then the noise: conversations layered over each other, tankards clinking, a bard in the corner working through something melancholy. The room is wood-dark and lamp-lit, smelling of stew and spilled ale.
key_features: the enormous hearthstone fireplace, blackened with decades of use
a long bar tended by a woman who remembers every face
private booths along the back wall, curtained for discretion

time_night.description_override: The Hearthstone comes alive after dark. Every table is taken. Voices compete with each other and the bard, who's found her groove now. The hearth throws long shadows and the room smells of roasted meat and too many people. This is where the city comes to forget the day.

name: Greyvale Ruins — Surface
description: Broken stone walls rise from the hillside like teeth from a jaw. Whatever stood here once was large — the footprint covers the entire hilltop. Most of it has been reclaimed by scrub and wildflowers. But the stairs going down are clear of growth, as if the earth itself refuses to cover them.
key_features: the main stairway descending into the ruins below
collapsed walls tracing the outline of a larger structure
wildflowers growing in patterns that follow the old foundation lines

name: Greyvale Ruins — Inner Chamber
description: Past the sealed door, the hum becomes a chord. The chamber is circular, walls covered in Aelindran notation so dense it looks like texture. In the center, a pedestal holds nothing — but the air above it shimmers, and the notation on the walls pulses faintly in response to your presence.
key_features: walls covered floor to ceiling in Aelindran academic notation
a central pedestal with a visible distortion in the air above it
scorch marks on the floor in a precise geometric pattern

name: Northern Greyvale
description: The forest goes wrong here. You notice it in the silence first — no birdsong, no insect hum. The wind moves the branches but stops at a boundary you can feel in your chest. Everything past the tree line has a stillness that doesn't belong to nature.

time_night.description_override: Darkness thickens the wrongness here. Every sound you make comes back louder than it should — your footsteps, your breathing. The tree line is a wall of black, and something in the distance reflects light that has no source.

name: South Road
description: Birdsong follows you out of the city, fading as the road narrows between barley fields. Cart ruts deepen in the mud. The pastoral quiet should be comforting, but the farms thin out too quickly heading north, and the last farmhouse you pass has its shutters closed in broad daylight.
atmosphere: open, pastoral, increasingly uneasy heading north

name: Millhaven Inn
description: The door scrapes against a warped floor. Inside, lamplight catches dust motes and the smell of old ale soaks into everything. A handful of locals nurse drinks at separate tables, conversations held low. The innkeeper watches the door like she's been counting who comes and who doesn't come back.

name: Torin's Quarters
description: Papers cover every surface — reports, maps, requisition forms stacked in towers that lean dangerously. The smell of ink and lamp oil hangs thick. Through the floorboards, you can hear the muffled business of the guild hall below. Torin's desk faces the door. Old habit.

name: Yanna's Farmhouse
description: Floorboards creak under your weight. A low fire crackles in the hearth, throwing warmth across a room that smells of dried herbs and bread cooling on a shelf. Everything here is worn but cared for — mended curtains, a swept floor, a chair with one leg shorter than the others.

name: Emris's Study
description: Parchment and books compete for every inch of space. The smell of old paper and salt air mixes where a window faces the harbor. Diagrams cover the walls — Aelindran notation, star charts, something that might be a map of places that don't exist anymore. A half-eaten meal sits forgotten on a stack of journals.

name: Grimjaw's Forge
description: Heat rolls out the open door in waves. Inside, the air shimmers. The forge takes up the back wall — a massive stone hearth fed by bellows that wheeze like something alive. Hammers hang from pegs, smallest to largest, each worn smooth. The smell is hot metal, coal smoke, and sweat. Every surface is scorched or scarred.
key_features: the great forge, stone-built and roaring
the bubbling hiss and sharp mineral smell of an alchemical laboratory behind a heat-shielded partition
a wall of weapons in various stages of completion
a workbench covered in metal scraps and half-finished projects

time_night.description_override: The forge is banked for the night. Embers glow in the hearth, casting long red shadows. The metal cools with soft pings and ticks. The smell of coal lingers.

name: Grimjaw's Quarters
description: A room behind and above the forge, reached by a narrow stone stair. Small, tidy in a way that suggests military habit. A cot bolted to the wall, a chest with three locks, and a shelf of metalworking texts. The heat from the forge below keeps it warm year-round. Through the floorboards, the faint tick of cooling metal.

name: The Old-Growth Grove
description: Birdsong pours down from a canopy too high to see, and the great trunks creak like ship timbers in a slow wind. The air smells of wet moss, crushed fern and old rain. Roots as thick as a horse's back knot the ground, and every step sinks into soft, deep loam. This forest is old, and it is listening.
key_features: a ring of standing stones swallowed by roots, older than any kingdom, their carvings worn smooth under your fingers
rope ladders and woven platforms high in the canopy, where Thyra's druids keep watch
a shrine to Thyra in the hollow of a living trunk, where travelers leave seed and water
thorn thickets along the northern edge that grow thicker and sharper toward the Ashmark

hidden_elements.description: the standing stones hum under your palm with a slow pulse — the forest's resistance to the Hollow is rooted here, deliberate and very old
knotted cords tied to the ladder rungs — the druids' tally of the days since the thorns last had to push the Hollow back

time_night.description_override: Night in the grove is louder, not quieter. Frogs and crickets fill the dark, and something large moves through the ferns without hurry. High above, a druid's lantern sways on its platform, the only light for miles.
time_night.atmosphere: thick dark, a chorus of night creatures, watched over

name: Keldaran Southern Pass
description: Wind howls through the pass and throws your footsteps back at you off bare stone. Somewhere below, a pickaxe rings in a steady rhythm, and the cold air tastes of iron and snowmelt. The trail climbs west between grey cliffs toward the Thornveld, marked by cairns of stacked stone.
key_features: stone cairns marking the trail every few hundred paces, each topped with a scrap of red cloth
the mouth of a working mine in the cliff face, where carts rattle out on iron rails
a waystation shrine shared by Aelora and Kaelen, a hearth-niche set beside a carved shield
a narrow ledge where the trail crosses a rockslide, loose scree shifting underfoot

hidden_elements.description: one cairn wears grey cloth instead of red — the miners' sign that something wrong was heard on the trail ahead, and that no one should camp past it
chisel marks on the freshly broken stone of the rockslide — the slope was cut loose on purpose, and recently

time_night.description_override: At night the wind drops to a low moan and the mine falls silent. Water drips somewhere in the rock, loud in the stillness. The only warmth is the waystation's hearth-niche, where someone has left a coal burning.
time_night.atmosphere: cold stillness, echoing drips, a single ember of welcome

name: The Tidal Shore
description: Gulls cry overhead, and surf breaks in long, hissing rushes over the shingle. The wind smells of salt, kelp and wet rope. Behind you the Accord's harbor bells ring faintly across the water, and ahead the shore curves north to where the rivers bleed into the sea.
atmosphere: open, salt-bright, the peaceful edge of the city
key_features: a tide line strewn with driftwood, kelp and broken crates washed out from the harbor
rock pools at the low-water mark, cold and full of scuttling things
a stone beacon tower where the harbor watch keeps a fire for ships at night
a fishers' shrine to Aelora, a cairn of white shells left for those lost at sea

hidden_elements.description: notches cut into a driftwood log above the tide line — a smugglers' count of crates run past the harbor watch
a damp watch ledger jammed into the beacon's base, its last entry complaining of oars heard rowing out on a night with no boat to row to

time_night.description_override: The surf sounds closer in the dark, each wave dragging the shingle back with a long rattle. The beacon fire crackles on its tower and sends a smell of pitch down the beach. Out on the black water, a bell buoy clangs with the swell.
time_night.atmosphere: dark water, rattling shingle, a lonely fire

name: The Reed Marsh
description: Water drips, laps and gurgles on every side, and insects whine in the reeds just out of reach. The air smells of rot and river silt, thick enough to taste. Fog sits low on the channels and muffles your footsteps until they sound like someone else's.
key_features: a maze of reed channels where the firm ground shifts with every tide
a stilt-house on the far bank, shutters closed, peat smoke drifting from its roof
the stone lip of a sunken building just under the black water, carved steps leading down into silt
a heron-post where marsh folk hang small bells to mark the safe crossing

hidden_elements.description: carvings on the sunken steps, felt more than seen beneath the silt — an old Aelindran library mark, and cut above it the sigil of Syrath's watchers, claiming the place as kept
one bell on the heron-post rings a half-tone flat — the marsh folk's warning that this crossing has been moved, and is not safe for strangers

time_night.description_override: At night the marsh fills with frogsong, a wall of croaking that stops all at once when you move. Something splashes in a channel and does not surface. Far off, the heron-post bells ring once, though there is no wind.
time_night.atmosphere: loud then silent, unseen movement, uncanny
